newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH FINMIN RESCINDS 16 INVESTMENT FUND LICENCES.
newsitem.headline: CZECH FINMIN RESCINDS 16 INVESTMENT FUND LICENCES.

text.p: The Czech finance ministry on Wednesday announced that it had rescinded the licences of 16 investment funds and two investment firms and fined 62 fund managers and investment companies in January.

Those losing licences included no major funds or investment companies, but the financial penalties were against large fund managers such as O.B. Invest, Sporitelni Investicni Spolecnost, and PPF Investicni Spolecnost, a ministry statement said.
In a statement, the ministry listed funds and firms which regulators ruled in January "had broken the law" on investment funds and companies.
They ranged from very small funds to large investment companies, but a spokeswoman declined to detail the offences or the extent of the punishment.
"You surely understand that we cannot give details on every company. It would be an unbearable amount of information," Finance Ministry spokeswoman Ludmila Nutilova, told Reuters.

"We have decided to publish the list of wrongdoers once a month and on request we can give further information," she said. When asked about one specific case, Sporitelni Investicni Spolecnost, she declined comment.
Regulators at the Finance Ministry's newly created Securities Bureau, referred all questions to Nutilova.
